structure_explanation.en: This is a short dialogue within Japanese quotation marks (「 」). In the first utterance, この店は marks "this shop" as the topic (with the particle は) and 初めて ("first time") closes the question without an explicit verb, with only question intonation marked by ？. In the reply, ええ is a colloquial "yes" and 初めてです repeats "it's the first time" now with the copula です to give a polite tone. The focus here is coverage (vocabulary and basic question/answer structure), and the sentence shows how Japanese often omits the verb when context makes it clear.

before.jp: あまり出かけたくなかった。

structure_explanation.en: The base is the verb 出かける (to go out). We take the stem 出かけ and add the auxiliary 〜たい (to want to do), forming 出かけたい (to want to go out). Since 〜たい conjugates just like an i-adjective, the negative-past becomes 〜たくなかった (did not want to), exactly the target くなかった: replace the final い with く and add なかった (negative past form). The adverb あまり (very/that much), combined with the negation, gives the sense of 'not very much'.

Como 〜たい se conjuga igual a um い-adjetivo, o negativo-passado vira 〜たくなかった (não queria), exatamente o foco-alvo くなかった: troca o い final por く e acrescenta なかった (forma negativa passada). O advérbio あまり (muito/tão), combinado com a negação, dá o sentido de 'não muito'.

structure_explanation.en: The heart of the sentence is 〜といいなあ: the clause 晴れてくれる ('to clear up, doing me that favor') + と + いい ('good') + なあ (particle of emotion). This pattern expresses a wish, 'I hope that / if only.' 晴れてくれる uses てくれる to show that good weather would be a favor to the speaker. (Note: the tokenizer split あした incorrectly; it is 明日 'tomorrow' as an adverb.)
structure_explanation.pt-BR: O coração da frase é 〜といいなあ: a oração 晴れてくれる ('clarear, fazendo-me esse favor') + と + いい ('bom') + なあ (partícula de emoção). Esse padrão expressa um desejo, 'tomara que / quem dera que'. 晴れてくれる usa てくれる para mostrar que o bom tempo seria um favor a quem fala. (Obs.: o tokenizador quebrou あした de forma incorreta; trata-se de 明日 'amanhã' como advérbio.)

ops.issue: 我 in the set expression 我の強い ('self-willed', JMdict: 我の強い【がのつよい】, cf. 我が強い ががつよい) is read が, not われ (archaic pronoun 'I').
我 meaning 'ego/self-will' in 我の強い／我が強い is read が; われ is the pronoun sense and wrong in this expression.
Romaji mirrors the wrong われ reading; should be ga no tsuyoi.
In 我の強いやつ, 我 is the subject of the attributive clause 我の強い (の substitutes が inside relative clauses); the modified nucleus is やつ, not 我. The role inverts the structure.

Restores locale parity with the en role: the pt-BR half had lost the statement that the modified head is やつ, which is the whole point of the inverted-head analysis, and it also spelled out の = が in shorthand rather than explaining the substitution.

before.jp: あいつは我の強いやつだ。
before.kana: あいつわわれのつよいやつだ。

structure_explanation.en: The topic is あいつ (that guy), marked by は. The descriptive core is 我の強い, literally 'of strong ego', a fixed expression in which 我 (ego, self-will) takes の and is qualified by 強い (strong); this whole block modifies やつ (subject/guy). The sentence closes with だ (copula 'is', informal). Result: 'a strong-willed guy', that is, stubborn/headstrong.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: O tópico é あいつ (aquele cara), marcado por は. O miolo descritivo é 我の強い, literalmente 'de ego forte', uma expressão fixa em que 我 (ego, vontade própria) leva の e é qualificado por 強い (forte); todo esse bloco modifica やつ (sujeito/cara). A frase fecha com だ (cópula 'é', informal). Resultado: 'um cara de vontade forte', ou seja, teimoso/cabeça-dura.

translation_literal.en: As for that guy, he's a strong-willed guy.

translation.pt-BR: Aquele cara é uma pessoa teimosa.
